title: Student Leader Devendra Mahto Stopped From Joining Tiranga Yatra in Ranchi Amid JPSC Exam Protests
excerpt: The JLKM leader, who has been on hunger strike over exam irregularities since August 2, was barred from attending a patriotic march in Ranchi ahead of Independence Day.
body:
• Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on hunger strike since August 2 over JPSC-JSSC exam irregularities, was stopped from attending a Tiranga Yatra in Ranchi ahead of Independence Day.
  • Mahto leads the Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) and has been protesting at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium since July 25, demanding CBI and ED investigations into paper leaks.
  • The student movement has drawn support from across the political spectrum, including BJP leader Babulal Marandi and activist Sonam Wangchuk, who intervened when Mahto's health deteriorated on Day 12.
  • Jharkhand's ruling JMM has promised a high-level committee to address the demands, but students say paper leaks have plagued the state's exam system for 26 years.

Student Leader Barred From Patriotic March

On the eve of India's 80th Independence Day, student leader Devendra Nath Mahto was prevented from participating in a Tiranga Yatra — a patriotic march carrying the national flag — in Ranchi, Jharkhand. The incident has drawn sharp criticism from student groups who say the irony of being barred from a freedom celebration while fighting for fair government recruitment is not lost on them.

https://x.com/DeccanHerald/status/2088556921661923470

Mahto, the leader of the Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM), has been at the center of a weeks-long agitation over alleged irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) examinations. He began an indefinite hunger strike on August 2 at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi, where students have held a round-the-clock sit-in since July 25.

"We have been on Satyagraha since July 25th. Papers have been leaking here for 26 years. Jobs are being sold off; every exam paper is getting leaked."

— Devendra Nath Mahto, JLKM leader

A Movement Rooted in Desperation

The protests erupted after results of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination were announced on July 5, with aspirants alleging widespread irregularities in the recruitment process. Students have demanded a proper investigation by the CBI and Enforcement Directorate into the JPSC examination, the JSSC Combined Graduate Level exam, and other recruitment tests.

Before launching his hunger strike, Mahto told reporters that the "lackadaisical attitude" of both central and state governments was demoralizing students and youth. In an emotional interview with The Indian Express, he revealed he lost his mother during an earlier phase of the JPSC movement. "Lost my mother fighting for the JPSC movement, but won't leave this fight," he said.

Health Crisis and Wangchuk's Intervention

By Day 12 of his hunger strike, Mahto's condition had deteriorated significantly. He said doctors warned him his blood sugar and blood pressure were dangerously low and his body was severely dehydrated. "My body organs are unable to cope," he told ET Digital.

Activist Sonam Wangchuk intervened through a video call, urging Mahto to take water. "Please take some water; this is tantamount to suicide," Wangchuk told him, adding that the government needed time but could respond in two to three weeks. Mahto agreed to take water and salt but said his hunger strike would continue in spirit.

Political Support and Government Response

The student movement has attracted support from across the political spectrum. A BJP delegation led by Jharkhand Leader of Opposition Babulal Marandi met Mahto at the protest site, adding a political dimension to the agitation. NSUI National President Vinod Jakhar and Congress MLA Abhimanyu Poonia also visited the protesting students.

The Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM), part of the ruling coalition under Chief Minister Hemant Soren, said it stands with the aspirants and promised a high-level committee within days. Governor Gangwar called the alleged irregularities a "very serious matter." Soren assured students that "no injustice will be allowed to happen."

Meanwhile, protesting students organized their own Tiranga march, demanding Soren's resignation over the continued sale of exam papers and jobs. "We are undertaking this Tiranga march, demanding the resignation of Chief Minister Hemant Soren, so that the selling of exam papers and jobs can be stopped," one protesting student told reporters.

What's Next

The agitation shows no signs of abating. Students have demanded that any government talks happen publicly in front of media, reflecting deep mistrust of behind-the-scenes negotiations. With Independence Day celebrations across the country, the juxtaposition of patriotic fervor and democratic protest in Ranchi has become a powerful symbol of the aspirations — and frustrations — of India's youth.
nri_angle: The JPSC-JSSC exam protests in Jharkhand highlight the ongoing governance challenges around government job recruitment that affect millions of Indian families, including those with members abroad.
